items.title: T3 Code Mobile 2.4 opens a remote dev server's localhost on the phone over a built-in tunnel, plus mobile issue trackers and reply citations
items.summary: The T3 Code mobile app can now render a coding agent's localhost preview natively on iOS or Android by tunnelling loopback traffic through the host environment, so you can check an agent's UI change from the phone without ngrok. It also adds issue trackers on mobile and highlight-to-comment citations on agent replies.

reception.summary: Users single out in-app localhost previews and citations as long-awaited; a few note they were stuck on an old TestFlight build and ask about iPad support and draft sync.

items.title: MacRemote 1.0: open-source Mac app that shares chosen local CLIs and MCP servers with any cloud agent over a permissioned tunnel
items.summary: Federico Viticci released MacRemote, a native macOS MCP host that exposes only the CLI tools and existing MCP servers you pick (it can import Claude Code, Codex and Cursor configs) to ChatGPT, Claude and other agents through a Cloudflare tunnel, with per-app approval, per-tool grants, ask-first for mutating tools and no shell access. Requires macOS 26.

doubt.pushback: Repliers ask whether revoking access mid-run cancels a running task and warn that exposing local tools to agents widens prompt-injection risk; GitHub reports the license as unasserted although the README says MIT.

reception.summary: Most replies praise the per-tool permission model; open questions on revoke-during-run behaviour, tailnet binding instead of a public tunnel, and how it compares with SSH.

items.title: Hands-on test of 16 agent browser and computer-use tools on one Apple Silicon Mac: cua-driver plus Ardia or OpenCode Browse win on speed, RAM and tokens
items.summary: Matt Van Horn timed 16 browser and Mac computer-use tools on the same five targets; cua-driver drove native apps in the background at about 27 MB RAM, and OpenCode Browse produced page snapshots 53x smaller than Stagehand while avoiding Chrome's remote-debugging prompts. Useful for anyone picking a browser layer for local coding agents.

doubt.pushback: Single-machine, author-run timings; a replier asks how the prompt-injection fences were actually scored, and another notes Chrome's own DevTools for agents covers much of this.

reception.summary: Mostly thanks and switch intentions; requests for a multi-agent concurrent run and for TinyFish and other tools in a second round.

items.title: OpenAI GPT-Live-1.1 debuts at #1 on Voice Arena's Jarvis Bench for naturalness, task effectiveness and 100% task success
items.summary: On live human-rated calls (2,442 votes), OpenAI's full-duplex GPT-Live-1.1 leads Jarvis Bench at 999 naturalness Elo and 1025 task-effectiveness Elo, and completes 100% of tasks when delegating to GPT 6.2 Sol Medium, ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking at 98%. The model is in the API as gpt-live-1.1 at $0.05 per active minute.

reception.summary: Few replies; they focus on the 100% task success and ask about delegation latency and whether the Sol Medium backend is configurable.

items.title: TensorFold 1.3.6 serves TFQ3 natively on CUDA: Qwen3.8-27B on a GB10 (DGX Spark) goes from 15.1 to 56.6 tok/s with speculative drafting
items.summary: TensorFold's 3, 4 and 5-bit TFQ3 quantized checkpoints now run on NVIDIA GPUs, with a linux-aarch64 build verified on GB10; with DFlash2 and DSpine drafters, Qwen3.8-27B decode rose 3.75x with bit-identical output in the author's coding test, and full GLM-5.3 runs on CUDA with MTP.

doubt.pushback: Speedups are the author's own single-task benchmark; no independent reproduction yet.

items.title: Cortheon v2: execution-verified parallel consensus runtime lifts frozen local models up to +30 points on AIME 2025
items.summary: Cortheon wraps a local model served by Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio or TensorFold with parallel generated Python, SymPy and Z3 checkers and consensus voting, with no weight changes; the author reports 3-bit GLM-5.3-Flash going from 50% to 80% on AIME 2025 and wins on all 8 benchmark runs across three model families, with per-problem logs in the repo.

doubt.pushback: Self-reported; AIME 2025 has 30 problems so 50 to 80 percent is 9 more answers, and gains come with many more inference calls per problem.

items.title: TontaubeV1.1 Flash: open Apache-2.0 TTS on Qwen3-0.6B that streams in real time on CPU in the browser via WebAssembly
items.summary: A small English text-to-speech model built on Qwen3-0.6B, with weights on Hugging Face, code on GitHub and a browser demo that runs on the CPU through WebAssembly, so speech synthesis needs no GPU or server.

doubt.pushback: No quality or latency numbers; very new and barely noticed (0 likes, 2 HF likes).
